findings.failure_path: A design using an ACL-authorized but poisoned knowledge source, prompt/template, adapter, tool schema, or agent skill can tick “data/model poisoning” through ACL/provenance labels and “supply chain” through model-artifact integrity. Neither mapping requires integrity validation for the poisoned source nor inventory/version verification for the non-model dependency, so the mandatory OWASP walk passes while manipulated inputs can still control model behavior or privileged actions.
findings.smallest_fix: Expand these two mappings into enforceable checks: validate and monitor authorized training/RAG sources for integrity and anomalous changes, and inventory, pin, verify, approve, and roll back every model, adapter, prompt/template, tool, skill, and package dependency—not only model artifacts.

challenge_focus: Attack the round-109 candidate on: (1) bypass-by-omission of the delegation fan-out gate (tick every item yet still fan out role-split slices? effort_budget prose-only?), the artifact-not-relay line, MAST classification, and the hub-vs-peer default; (2) zero-loss of the four retired cost sub-bullets and the shortened required_skills rationale; (3) contradictions between new llm-inference text and existing rules: dynamic tool search vs never-change-tools-mid-loop, batch endpoints vs bounded concurrency and spend caps, goodput vs the p50/p95/p99 checklist, judge-bias controls vs freeze-before-run and contamination rules, lethal-trifecta vs existing injection and side-effect authorization rules; (4) vendor numbers stated as invariants, stale claims, wrong arXiv ids or dates; (5) over-broad absolutes that tax a simple single-agent delivery or a keyless eval lane; (6) private-path or organization-noun leakage; (7) completeness of the OWASP walk and the serving-lever metric mapping.
